assumptions: FX: USD→INR ₹95.7 (Wise/exchangerates.org.uk, 14 Sep 2026; the docs used ₹95.5). EUR→INR ₹110.9 (exchangerates.org.uk, 12 Sep 2026) for Hetzner lines. All figures are monthly steady state, ex-GST, and exclude Vercel/Supabase/Cloudflare-DNS which are identical on both sides.

Product assumptions are taken verbatim from docs/SCALE-PLAN.md §1 (60-wedding mix: 10×10 GB, 20×20 GB, 20×40 GB, 10×60 GB Cinema) so the two sides are comparable: 31.7 GB of encoded ladder stored per wedding (1,900 GB/60), 85.8 GB delivered per wedding (5,146 GB/60, i.e. 300 guests × 20 min at 0.26 GB per session, PRICING-MODEL.md 'Redoing' table), 10 min of 4K premium encoding per wedding on average (600 min/60; one wedding in six is Cinema with 60 min 4K), ~835 source minutes to encode per wedding (allocated GB ÷ 2.15 GB/hr, lib/entitlements.ts:131 GB_PER_HOUR.standard = 2.15). Live storage is held for 12 months per wedding (SCALE-PLAN §4.1: 3,800 GB at end of year one for 10/month), so stored GB = weddings/month × 12 × 31.7.

CODE OVERRIDES THE DOCS on storage: lib/video/bunny.ts:198-201 states the library keeps originals and has MP4 fallback ON (checked against the account API), and docs/PRICING.md §5 (6 Sep) prices on 'originals + renditions ≈30% on top' — Keep is costed at 130 GB/yr, Cinema 260 GB/yr. SCALE-PLAN §6 item 2 ('confirm Keep Originals and MP4 Fallback are off') is therefore stale. The model above uses SCALE-PLAN's ladder-only 31.7 GB for comparability; if originals are kept, multiply BOTH storage lines by roughly 3–4×. That widens Bunny's lead with R2 ($0.015 vs $0.01/GB) and narrows it with B2 ($0.00695/GB) but does not move the breakeven verdict.

CODE OVERRIDES THE DOCS on delivery metering: lib/video/bunny.ts:234-261 derives deliveredGb from Bunny's per-video watchTimeChart × GB_PER_HOUR.standard (N-25, supabase/migrations/0015_usage_watch_seconds.sql), so SCALE-PLAN §4.2's 'deliveredGb: 0' is out of date. Per-catalogue delivery is still an estimate, not measured bandwidth — Bunny only exposes bandwidth per pull zone. A self-hosted pipeline would get real per-object bytes from CDN logs, which is a genuine (non-cost) benefit.

The 4K minute allowance is NOT enforced in code: no file under lib/ app/ components/ references 2160/1440/premium or sets enabledResolutions (grep, 15 Sep). Resolutions are a library-wide Bunny setting, so the $0.15/min line is a policy estimate, not a metered one. 4K encoding is the one Bunny line self-hosting removes entirely (₹1,436 → ₹1,43,550/month across the four scenarios).

Bunny rates (bunny.net/docs/stream/pricing, 15 Sep 2026): storage $0.01/GB-month (Frankfurt default; the library's storage is in Singapore per lib/photos/bunny.ts:16-17 — Bunny has no India origin, Mumbai is 'planned' on the storage page), Standard-tier delivery Asia & Oceania $0.030/GB (the Volume tier at $0.005/GB has 10 PoPs and no India PoP — PRICING-MODEL §6 rightly rejects it for the 1.5 s-on-4G promise), standard encoding free, premium 2160p/1440p $0.150/min, $1 monthly minimum. Token auth, TUS upload, webhooks, HLS packaging and thumbnails carry no separate charge — the code uses all of them (bunny.ts:74-93 TUS signature, :96-148 directory-scoped token, :264-305 HMAC webhook, :181-189 thumbnail_N.jpg posters).

Self-hosted stack modelled: Hetzner Cloud workers (CCX33 8 dedicated vCPU/32 GB €48.49, CCX23 €31.49, 20–30 TB egress included, €1/TB after; prices post 15 Jun 2026 increase) for TUS ingest (tusd, open source) and FFmpeg; Hetzner GEX44 (RTX 4000 SFF Ada, €184/month + €79 setup; listed as out of stock Jul 2026 — fallback AWS g4dn.xlarge Mumbai $0.577/hr, whose T4 NVENC is roughly half the throughput) from 300 weddings/month; object storage on Cloudflare R2 ($0.015/GB-month Standard, $0 egress) as the primary figure, with Backblaze B2 ($6.95/TB-month, free egress to Cloudflare and Bunny under the Bandwidth Alliance) as the cheap variant in the notes; delivery through Cloudflare CDN (Pro $25 to 60/month, Business $250 above) with a Workers Paid ($5 + $0.30/M requests) edge for signed-URL checks, 300 sessions × 200 six-second segments per wedding; Better Stack/Grafana Cloud monitoring $29–100. Job queue reuses the existing Postgres (lib/jobs/run.ts already has a job runner), so no extra line.

Encoding throughput assumptions (order-of-magnitude, from public NVENC/x264 guidance, not benchmarked): CPU x264 on 8 dedicated vCPU produces the 360/480/720p ladder at ~1.5× real time from a 1080p source and a 4K ladder at ~0.3×; one RTX 4000 Ada NVENC does the standard ladder at ~8× real time and 4K at ~2.5× (2–3 concurrent 4K streams). Boxes are sized at 1.3× monthly average for seasonal bursts (Indian weddings cluster Nov–Feb; the monthly average understates peak). AWS MediaConvert at $0.015/min HD Basic (US East example rates; Mumbai not published per-minute) would cost more than Bunny's free standard encoding at every scale and is excluded.

Two self-hosted risks are not priced but would decide it: (1) Cloudflare's own 'Delivering Videos with Cloudflare' page says video through the CDN on self-serve plans is restricted to Stream/Stream Delivery (Enterprise), while its May 2023 ToS blog says R2-hosted video is permitted — at 26–86 TB/month (300–1,000 weddings) expect an Enterprise conversation costing lakhs a year, which would roughly double the 'cdn' line; Cloudflare's India ISP peering on self-serve plans is also weaker than Bunny's India PoPs. The safe alternative — a Bunny CDN pull zone in front of your own origin — keeps delivery at the same $0.03/GB you pay today, so self-hosting then saves only storage and 4K encoding. (2) Neither R2 (APAC location hint) nor B2 (US/EU only) nor Hetzner (EU only) has an Indian origin, so cache-miss first plays on a cold edge will be slower than Bunny's Singapore-origin setup; CloudFront India ($0.109/GB first 9 TB after 1 TB free, $0.085 next 40 TB) is 3–4× Bunny and never wins.

People cost (INR/month, India, from 2026 salary guides: SRE average ₹11–14 LPA, mid-level DevOps ₹18–35 LPA at product companies): 0.2 FTE ₹35,000 at 10/month (retained freelancer, but someone must be on call for a wedding-night outage), 0.4 FTE ₹70,000 at 60, one full-time SRE at ~₹24 LPA ₹2,00,000 at 300 (incl. on-call cover), two people (SRE + media engineer) ₹4,00,000 at 1,000. Today's Bunny path has effectively zero dedicated ops headcount — reconcile cron (app/api/cron/reconcile/route.ts) and synthetic probe (app/api/cron/synthetic/route.ts) already cover the failure modes.

One-off build (note, not in the monthly figures): a TUS server with S3 multipart backend, FFmpeg worker fleet with the ladder/thumbnail/seek-VTT outputs the player expects (bunny.ts:130-131 seek.vtt, thumbnail_N.jpg), HLS packaging, signed-URL edge, queue, retries, monitoring, plus re-implementing VideoProvider (lib/video/provider.ts, 5 methods — the seam exists) and migrating the live library (egress of every original out of Bunny at Asia rates) — roughly 8–12 engineer-weeks, ₹6–9 lakh at Indian contract rates, plus €79 per GPU box setup. That build must also reproduce what components/admin/UploadManager.tsx relies on: tus offset resume from the server's acked offset (lines 67-83), which CLAUDE.md flags as the place the schedule slips.

Bunny numbers at 300 and 1,000 weddings/month are list price. At 26–86 TB/month of delivery and 114–380 TB stored, SCALE-PLAN §5 already says to negotiate a committed contract past ~10 TB/month; any discount there moves the breakeven further out.

scenarios.name: 10 weddings/month (SCALE-PLAN's current plan)
scenarios.notes: Bunny: 3,800 GB stored $38 + 858 GB delivered $26 + 100 min 4K $15 = $79. Self-hosted infra (R2): storage $57 + Cloudflare Pro/Workers $30 + 1× CCX33 encoder (98 box-hours, ~14% utilised) €48 + 1× CCX23 tusd ingest €31 + monitoring $29 = $209 = ₹19,971; with B2 storage ₹17,044. Including people, self-hosting costs ₹54,971 vs ₹7,534 — 7.3× dearer. The fixed floor of a two-box pipeline is already larger than the whole Bunny bill.

scenarios.name: 60 weddings/month (the six-month target run monthly)
scenarios.notes: Bunny: 22,800 GB $228 + 5,148 GB delivered $154 + 600 min 4K $90 = $472. Self-hosted infra (R2): storage $342 + CDN $30 + 2× CCX33 encoders (590 box-hours; one box would run at 82% with no burst headroom) €97 + 1× CCX33 ingest €48 + monitoring $29 = $570 = ₹54,508; B2 variant ₹36,944 (the only line where B2 beats Bunny infra-only, by ₹8k). With people: ₹1,24,508 (R2) or ₹1,06,944 (B2) against Bunny ₹45,207 — 2.4–2.8× dearer.

scenarios.name: 300 weddings/month (Vercel's function-invocation ceiling per SCALE-PLAN §3)
scenarios.notes: Bunny: 114 TB $1,140 + 25.7 TB delivered $772 + 3,000 min 4K $450 = $2,362 (list; a committed contract would be lower). Self-hosted infra (R2): storage $1,710 + Cloudflare Business + Workers (18M segment requests) $257 + 2× GEX44 GPU boxes (542 GPU-hours, one box at 75% plus a spare) €368 + 2× CCX33 ingest €97 + monitoring $100 = $2,606 = ₹2,49,416; B2 variant ₹1,61,593. With one full-time SRE: ₹4,49,416 (R2) or ₹3,61,593 (B2) vs Bunny ₹2,26,034 — still 1.6–2.0× dearer. 26 TB/month of video through Cloudflare Business is where its video-delivery terms become a live risk.

scenarios.name: 1,000 weddings/month
scenarios.notes: Bunny: 380 TB $3,800 + 85.8 TB delivered $2,573 + 10,000 min 4K $1,500 = $7,873 (list; at this volume a negotiated rate is near-certain). Self-hosted infra (R2): storage $5,700 + CDN $270 + 4× GEX44 (1,806 GPU-hours) €736 + 3× CCX33 ingest (40 TB/month ingress, NVMe staging) €145 + monitoring $100 = $7,091 = ₹6,78,654 — the first scenario where infra alone is below Bunny (by ₹75k, all of it the 4K encoding line). B2 variant ₹3,85,908. With two people (₹4,00,000): ₹10,78,654 (R2) or ₹7,85,908 (B2) vs Bunny ₹7,53,446 — Bunny is still cheaper, by ₹3.25 lakh (R2) or ₹32k (B2). 86 TB/month through Cloudflare self-serve would almost certainly force an Enterprise contract, not priced here.

breakeven: No breakeven inside the modelled range once people are included. Infrastructure alone crosses at roughly 900–1,000 weddings/month (R2 stack) or ~50–60 weddings/month (B2 + Cloudflare stack, storage-only saving), but the cheapest honest ops headcount — ₹35k/month at 10 weddings rising to ₹4 lakh at 1,000 — is larger than the whole Bunny bill until ~300 weddings/month and larger than the infra saving at every scale tested. The curves only touch at ~1,000 weddings/month under the most aggressive assumptions (B2 storage at $6.95/TB with free egress, video delivered through Cloudflare self-serve at $0 egress, GEX44s in stock, ladder-only storage with originals not kept, two-person team) — ₹7.86 lakh vs Bunny's list-price ₹7.53 lakh — and at that volume Bunny would be on a negotiated contract (SCALE-PLAN §5 says to open that past 10 TB/month; you would be at 86 TB), which pushes the crossing out again. Extrapolating the B2 stack linearly, self-hosting including people becomes cheaper only somewhere past ~1,500 weddings/month, and only if Cloudflare tolerates ~130 TB/month of video on a Business plan, which its own policy page says it will not. The unit economics reason is structural: Bunny's marginal cost per wedding at list is $7.87 (₹753), of which $2.57 is delivery at India-PoP rates that no self-hosted CDN with Indian PoPs beats (CloudFront India is 3.6× Bunny; Cloudflare is $0 only if the ToS holds), $3.80 is storage at $0.01/GB that only B2/Hetzner Object Storage undercut and neither has an Indian region, and $1.50 is 4K encoding — the one line self-hosting removes cleanly. Recommendation the numbers support: stay on Bunny, keep lib/video/provider.ts as the swap seam, and spend the effort on the two things the code shows are unfinished — enforcing the 4K minute allowance at upload (nothing in code sets resolutions) and deciding whether keep-originals/MP4-fallback (on, per lib/video/bunny.ts:198-201) is meant, since that setting is worth more per month than any provider change.
